blocks.text: NAGOYA, Japan — Philippines tennis trailblazer Alexandra Eala was in ruthless mood at the Asian Games on Monday as rain disrupted some events and Japanese organisers faced renewed accusations of mismanagement. Eala launched her title charge with victory in just 55 minutes against the outclassed world number 517 Patcharin Cheapchandej. Eala, ranked 18 and favourite for gold in Nagoya, thrashed the Thai 6-1, 6-0, after the bad weather delayed the start and forced the match inside onto a smaller court. Top seed Eala will face Taiwan’s UK-born eighth seed Joanna Garland in the quarter-finals. READ: Alex Eala cruises into Asian Games […]...
